- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 2–5%.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast decline, true price often rebounds — adjust downward peak to match prior trend.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.3) and model forecasts rise, it’s likely overconfident; cap upward moves at 1–3% above recent mean.
- Model often underestimates late-period price increases (last 5–7 days of forecast) — increase final 3–5 days by 1–3% to align with true outcome.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating high/low), model tends to lag — forecast should be adjusted to match sentiment direction 1–2 days ahead.
- If model forecast mean is consistently below true outcome mean, add 0.5–1.5% to forecast mean for next period, especially if sentiment is bullish.
- If sentiment is high but model forecast is flat or declining, model is underreacting — increase forecast slope to match sentiment momentum.
